competing_hypotheses.support: The immediately prior answer explained concepts without fresh evidence of cognition execution.
competing_hypotheses.falsification: Repeated user corrections plus the evaluator implementation show a reusable path where report labels can pass without admission evidence.

competing_hypotheses.support: session_adherence.py parses report labels and state contradictions but, before this candidate, has no RootScopeReceipt or EvolutionDisposition evidence binding.
competing_hypotheses.falsification: The kernel already exposes typed RootScopeReceipt and EvolutionDisposition, so the gap can be closed without a second cognition controller or new SOP.

competing_hypotheses.support: Repeated live failures could suggest the policy never required cognition before problem closure.
competing_hypotheses.falsification: Session 1.9 already requires the canonical cognition transaction and root-scope/evolution admission before problem closure.

competing_hypotheses.support: Host-level interception could provide stronger non-bypassability.
competing_hypotheses.falsification: The observed false-positive can be explained and detected at the assurance layer without proving host interception is necessary.

candidate_change.mechanism: When cognition admission is required, report text cannot self-prove execution. The evaluator separately requires a typed RootScopeReceipt, a typed EvolutionDisposition, and a problem_record_ref when the receipt requires durable evidence.
candidate_change.anti_bloat: No Session policy expansion, no new controller, no duplicated cognition state machine, no extra mandatory user-facing report field.
